sources.citation: Reed, Lauren W. 2019. Sign Languages of Western Highlands, Papua New Guinea, and their Challenges for Sign Language Typology. MA thesis, Australian National University. 167 pp. (hdl 1885/165444)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Zero hits for stress/accent/suprasegmental/intonation; the only 'prosodic' mention (c. p.50) concerns spoken Ku Waru speech genres. On phonology it says (p.4) 'these young SLs do not have a stable phonological system' and (p.62) 'It seems that the signing in this area does not exhibit phonological contrast below the level of the word.' Appendix C covers phonological reduction (handshape/location), not prominence.
